lessons.title: Planning the store layout
lessons.html:
What is merchandising?

Merchandising means placing and showing goods so customers find them easily and want to buy them. A well-merchandised agri store is clean, tidy and easy to walk through. Farmers are busy. If they can find what they need quickly, they will come back.

Group products that belong together

  • Animal health: dips, dewormers, syringes, ear tags and tag applicators together.
  • Fencing: wire, droppers, straining posts, fencing pliers and gate hinges together.
  • Garden and vegetables: seed packets, small fertiliser bags, hosepipes and watering cans.
  • Protective clothing: gloves, overalls, boots, masks and goggles.

When things that are used together are close, customers often buy more. A farmer who buys a dewormer may also need a dosing gun.

Where to place items

  • Eye level is where customers look first. Put popular items and specials there.
  • Heavy items go on the bottom shelf or on the floor on pallets, for safety.
  • Small, costly items like pocket knives or medicines may be kept near the till or behind the counter to stop theft.
  • Chemicals on display must still be kept away from feed and food and follow the store's rules. Many stores keep only empty display containers on the floor.

Keep walkways open

Leave aisles wide enough for trolleys and for people to pass. Do not leave boxes in the walkway. Fire exits and extinguishers must always be clear and easy to see.

lessons.title: Building and keeping displays
lessons.html:
Making a good display

  1. Clean the shelf first. Wipe dust and remove old stickers.
  2. Check you have enough stock to fill the space.
  3. Pack items with the label facing the customer. We call this "facing".
  4. Put the same item in a neat block, not spread around.
  5. Put older stock in front (first in, first out).
  6. Put the correct shelf label under each product.
  7. Step back and look as a customer would. Is it neat? Can you read the prices?

Seasonal displays

Change the main display with the farming season.

SeasonDisplay ideas
Spring (planting)Seed, fertiliser, planter spares
Summer (rain)Dips, fly control, dewormers
Autumn and winterLick, feed, fire-break tools, warm clothing

Point-of-sale material

Posters, price cards and "special" signs help sell. Use only approved material from your manager or supplier. Signs must be neat, correct and taken down when the special ends.

Keeping it tidy

  • Walk the store at least twice a day.
  • Fill empty spaces from the store room.
  • Put back items customers left in the wrong place.
  • Remove damaged or expired stock.
  • Report empty shelves where no stock is left, so it can be ordered.

Safety

Do not stack displays too high. Make sure nothing can fall on a customer. Use a ladder, not a shelf, to reach high places.

Key points

  • Group products that are used together.
  • Popular items at eye level, heavy items low.
  • Face labels to the customer and keep prices correct.
  • Change displays with the season.
  • Keep aisles and fire exits clear.
